brief: An herb amphitheatre for a kitchen window: three staggered rows of three planters stepping up one, two and three storeys from front to back, so every plant faces the viewer at the low side. Front row: thyme, oregano and alyssum. Middle row: basil, parsley and chives. Back row: rosemary, sage and mint. Fill every planter with soil and plant it. Put the one-storey row nearest the default view and the tall row farthest from it, and use look to check that every plant is visible from that view.

requirements.evidence: 9 base cells in a 3x3 block at level 0 (q -1..1, r -1..1); middle band (r=0) built up to level 1, back band (r=-1) to level 2; front band (r=1) stays one storey
requirements.requirement: Three staggered rows of three planters stepping 1, 2, 3 storeys front to back

requirements.evidence: Low row (r=1, level 0) includes cell 1,1 nearest the default-view camera (az 45, +x+z); tall 3-storey row at r=-1 farthest; look at az 45 polar 62 and polar 10 lists all 9 plant props seen

finish.summary: Herb amphitheatre built: 3x3 base stepping from 1 storey (front, r=1) to 2 (middle, r=0) to 3 (back, r=-1), one full-depth planter per cell, all 9 filled with soil and planted as briefed. Default-view looks confirm all 9 plants visible; check_build passes with meshClash clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
